metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets The Palestinian Authority

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for the Palestinian Authority using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported uncertainty (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicates that the OECD’s standard complex-survey estimation procedures were used when computing means, differences, and correlations.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a results factsheet that reports descriptive and comparative statistics (means on a 60-point scale, proficiency level shares, and relative success differences) rather than providing an analysis pipeline with explicit plausible-value (PV) generation/combining and missing-data handling steps. While PISA achievement scales are typically based on PVs, the factsheet text provided does not state how PVs were handled for these reported indicators, nor does it describe any missing-data procedure. Therefore, the PV and missing-data handling information is not available in the excerpt, representing a reporting gap for methodological transparency at the factsheet level.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports that, in the Palestinian Authority, 7,905 students in 273 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 88,400 15-year-olds (estimated 78% of the total population of 15-year-olds). The excerpt does not specify additional analytic exclusions (e.g., creative-thinking-only completion, item-level completion thresholds, or missing background questionnaire rules), so the analytic sample is treated as the available PISA 2022 student sample for the Palestinian Authority used for the reported creative thinking indicators.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for 15-year-old students in the Palestinian Authority. It reports an overall mean score of 18 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly below the OECD average (33), and provides proficiency-level distributions (31% reaching at least Level 3; 6% at Level 5 or 6). The factsheet also describes relative performance patterns across ideation processes (generating creative ideas vs generating diverse ideas; evaluating and improving ideas) and across domain contexts (written, visual, social problem solving, scientific problem solving), using “relative success” differences that account for task difficulty. It further highlights within-country gaps: socio-economic status predicts creative thinking (explaining 6% of variation), and girls outperform boys by 5.9 score points. Methodologically, the excerpt does not provide an ML modeling approach or explicit PV/missing-data procedures, so the results should be interpreted as OECD’s standardized PISA reporting rather than as outputs from a bespoke predictive model.
